tagline.en: The Long Island Expressway — the world's longest parking lot
tagline.zh: 长岛快速路——“世界上最长的停车场”

mileageSource: FHWA Route Log and Finder List, Table 2, January 2026

start.zh: 曼哈顿，皇后区—中城隧道

end.en: County Route 58 at Riverhead, Suffolk County
end.zh: 萨福克县里弗黑德，接 58 号县道

en: The Long Island Expressway starts at the Manhattan portal of the Queens–Midtown Tunnel, runs under the East River, and then heads east for the length of Long Island: across Queens, through Nassau County, and out through Suffolk to Riverhead, where it stops at a county road. It is numbered as though it were a loop off I-95, which is what an even hundreds digit is supposed to mean. It is not one. It leaves and never comes back, and it is one of the clearest cases in the system of the numbering convention being honoured in name only.

For most of its length it is the only limited-access road serving the island's spine, which is the whole problem. There is no parallel freeway to take the overflow, the crossings at the western end are the only way off the island by car, and the expressway's counts show it: between exits 33 and 34 it carried an average of 184,984 vehicles a day in 2023. Drivers have called it the world's longest parking lot since at least 1963.
zh: 长岛快速路的起点是皇后区—中城隧道的曼哈顿一侧洞口，穿过东河后一路向东，贯穿整个长岛：横过皇后区，穿越拿骚县，再经萨福克县抵达里弗黑德，在那里接上一条县道便结束。它的编号用的是偶数百位，按惯例应当表示一条离开母线后再回到 I-95 的环线。但它不是。它一去不返，是全系统中编号惯例只剩下名义的最清楚的例子之一。
它在大部分路段都是服务长岛中脊的唯一一条全封闭道路，问题正出在这里。没有平行的高速可以分流，西端的过河通道又是开车离开长岛的唯一出口，交通量数据说明了一切：2023 年 33 号与 34 号出口之间的日均交通量为 184,984 辆。至迟从 1963 年起，司机们就把它叫作「世界上最长的停车场」。

en: The road was built in pieces over thirty-two years. The first piece was the Queens–Midtown Tunnel, which opened on 15 November 1940; the highway connecting it to Laurel Hill Boulevard was built at about the same time. Construction then stopped for the war and resumed under Robert Moses, whose Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority built the Queens sections in the 1950s. The first section on Long Island proper, in Nassau County, opened in October 1958.

Funding split the road in two administratively: most of the Queens mileage was built as Interstate work, 90 per cent federal and 10 per cent state, while the Nassau and Suffolk sections were funded equally by the federal and state governments. The last 2.1 miles, past Calverton to Riverhead, opened in June 1972. The New York Times marked the occasion by noting that the road had been under construction for thirty-two years and was already carrying 150,000 cars a day.
zh: 这条路是分段修了三十二年。第一段是皇后区—中城隧道，1940 年 11 月 15 日通车；把隧道与劳雷尔希尔大道连起来的公路也差不多同时建成。此后因战争停工，战后在罗伯特·摩西手下重启，由他主持的三区桥梁与隧道管理局在 1950 年代修建了皇后区各段。长岛本岛上的第一段位于拿骚县，1958 年 10 月通车。
资金来源把这条路在行政上分成了两半：皇后区的大部分里程按州际公路标准建设，联邦出九成、州出一成；拿骚县与萨福克县路段则由联邦与州各出一半。最后 2.1 英里从卡尔弗顿延至里弗黑德，于 1972 年 6 月通车。《纽约时报》在报道中提到，这条路已经修了三十二年，而当时它每天已经承载 15 万辆汽车。

en: The expressway was congested before it was finished. In August 1963 the New York Times was describing a road prescribed less than ten years earlier as a remedy for the region's post-war traffic problems, and now 'part and parcel of the ailment' — while nearly half of it was still unbuilt east of Nassau County. The nickname dates from the same period and has never come off.

The modern counts are steadier than the reputation suggests. Between exits 33 and 34, the busiest point measured on Long Island, the daily average was 184,984 vehicles in 2023, up 2.6 per cent on 2022 and almost exactly back to the 185,670 recorded in 2019 before the pandemic. The road is full, in other words, in the specific sense that it has been at about the same very high number for years: demand is limited by the capacity of the pavement rather than the other way round.
zh: 这条快速路在建成之前就已经堵了。1963 年 8 月，《纽约时报》写道，这条不到十年前还被当作战后交通问题「药方」的公路，如今已经「成了病症本身的一部分」——而当时拿骚县以东还有将近一半没有修。那个绰号也出自同一时期，此后再没摘掉。
今天的交通量数据比它的名声要平稳。33 号与 34 号出口之间是长岛上实测最繁忙的点位，2023 年日均 184,984 辆，比 2022 年上升 2.6%，几乎正好回到疫情前 2019 年的 185,670 辆。换句话说，这条路的「满」有一层具体含义：多年来它一直停在差不多同一个很高的数字上，是路面通行能力限制了需求，而不是反过来。

figures.source: FHWA Route Log and Finder List, Table 2, January 2026

why.en: No consolidated figure exists. The expressway was built between 1940 and 1972 by several different bodies under different funding formulas — city, state, the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority and the federal Interstate programme — and costs were accounted for contract by contract.
why.zh: 没有汇总数据。这条快速路自 1940 年至 1972 年由多个不同机构按不同的出资比例分段建成——包括市政府、州政府、三区桥梁与隧道管理局以及联邦州际公路计划——费用是按合同分别核算的。

value.en: 184,984 vehicles a day between exits 33 and 34, up 2.6 per cent on 2022
value.zh: 33 号与 34 号出口之间每日 184,984 辆，较 2022 年上升 2.6%

trafficFigures.source: Newsday, analysis of New York State DOT counts, 2023 data

label.en: Traffic when the road was completed

timeline.en: The Queens–Midtown Tunnel opens, the first piece of what becomes I-495.
timeline.zh: 皇后区—中城隧道通车，成为日后 I-495 的第一段。

timeline.en: The first section on Long Island proper opens in Nassau County.
timeline.zh: 长岛本岛上的第一段在拿骚县通车。

timeline.en: With the eastern half still unbuilt, the press is already calling the expressway the world's longest parking lot.
timeline.zh: 东半段尚未修建，媒体已称这条快速路为「世界上最长的停车场」。

timeline.en: The final 2.1 miles to Riverhead open, ending thirty-two years of construction.
timeline.zh: 通往里弗黑德的最后 2.1 英里通车，三十二年的工程结束。
